key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN workflow can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE, revealing that bottom preheating stabilizes forces, raises temperatures, and reduces defect risk.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a practical process map for selecting welding speed, rotation speed, and preheating settings to improve weld integrity and avoid wormholes in thermoplastic joining.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force data
Process-window comparison across rotational speed, travel speed, and bottom preheating conditions
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved R2 values of 0.91–0.99, and the CEL results matched experiments for void formation, thermal response, and mechanical force trends.
watch_item: The process map is based on a limited tested parameter space, so broader materials, tool geometries, and operating ranges may require retraining or revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
